correctness.rationale: For a nonzero pair-sum (x,y), both coordinates are nonzero, and the representing parameters are the roots of Z²−xZ+x/y; the only exceptional fiber is (0,0), exactly the ordered antipodal pairs. Character orthogonality gives q²Q/n⁴ for the output fourth power, while the input fourth power is M²/n². Counting diagonal and distinct pairs with their ordered multiplicities gives Q=2M²−Σ(A_t²+|B_t|²/2)+|B|². Expanding the centered sums using ΣA_t=M and ΣB_t=B gives the stated identity with k=n/2, including k=1. The last term is nonnegative by |B|≤Σ2|f(t)f(−t)|≤M. If the deficit is zero for nonzero f, the equal A_t and |B|=M force each pair to have equal moduli and all coefficients to have the same positive modulus; equal B_t gives the common product. The converse and attainment by a constant function follow directly. The proof works for every odd prime power; the frozen checker was inspected but not run and only supplies finite diagnostics.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Expand Σ(A_t−M/k)² and (1/2)Σ|B_t−B/k|² by subtracting M²/k and |B|²/(2k) from the raw squares, respectively. Adding (1−1/(2k))(M²−|B|²) leaves (1−3/(2k))M²+ΣA_t²+(1/2)Σ|B_t|²−|B|², exactly the sharp bound minus the earlier identity. The nonnegativity uses |B|≤M, already a triangle and pairwise AM–GM inequality. This mechanically implies the new display from the earlier weighted formula even though the earlier text does not print that display.
